column3: BSB renders “as slaves” as “of slavery” and “the teaching” as “our teaching.”
BSB reads “those receiving their good service are beloved believers,” taking the masters as the ones who benefit.
BSB renders “does not draw near to” as “disagrees with” and “the teaching according to godliness” as “godly teaching.”
BSB starts a new sentence with “Instead” and renders “disputes about words” as “semantics.”
BSB follows the critical text, which lacks the Textus Receptus clause “withdraw from such”; it starts a new sentence with “These men.”
BSB adds “Of course.”
BSB follows the critical text without “it is evident” (δῆλον), which the Textus Receptus adds; “so” renders “because.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB renders “into temptation and a snare” as “fall into temptation and become ensnared.”
BSB renders “a root of all kinds of evils” as “the root.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB adds “when” before “you made the good confession.”
BSB adds “in His testimony.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB renders “will display” as “will bring about.”
BSB renders “alone having immortality” as “alone is immortal.”
BSB follows the critical text with “in God”; the Textus Receptus has “in the living God.”
BSB adds “Instruct them.”
BSB follows the critical text with “truly life” (ὄντως); the Textus Receptus reads “eternal life.” “Firm” is added.
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “with you all” and no “Amen”; the Textus Receptus has “with you” (singular), “Amen,” and a closing note about writing from Laodicea.
